samples.summary: The 401 session-eviction redirect is refusable (and then permanently latched off) by the `beforeunload` guard this PR adds
samples.evidence: This delta states the invariant that "an app-issued redirect has to *be* a replace" so it cannot be refused (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:151-161), and fixes `PrivateRoute`/`PublicRoute` accordingly. The same invariant is violated by the other, non-router eviction path this PR newly made refusable. `fetchWithAuth` on a 401 calls `logout({redirect:false,...})` then `redirectTo("/login")` (api/auth.ts:153-160). `redirectTo` sets the module-level latch `isRedirecting = true` *before* assigning `window.location.href` (auth.ts:28-30). Earlier commits of this PR registered a `beforeunload` handler that calls `event.preventDefault()` whenever the document has unsent edits (components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.tsx:92-103). A script-initiated `location.href` assignment fires `beforeunload`, so the browser shows the native "Leave site?" dialog; if the user picks "Cancel/Stay", the navigation to /login is aborted while `isRedirecting` stays `true` for the life of the tab. From then on every subsequent 401 in the session early-returns from `redirectTo` (auth.ts:28) and the thrown `AuthExpiredError` is deliberately swallowed by callers (e.g. app/templates/template-landing.tsx:116), so the expired session never evicts: the authenticated shell and the previously-fetched document content stay rendered indefinitely — a real exposure on a shared machine. Attacker/vector: any user (or an attacker who reaches an unattended tab) leaves an editor in the "not saved" state, waits for session expiry, and answers "Stay" once. I could not exercise a real browser to confirm the abort leaves the latch set, hence low confidence; the code path itself is traceable line by line. Fix would be to clear `isRedirecting` on a cancelled navigation (e.g. reset it in a `pagehide`/timeout) or to not latch before the assignment.

samples.summary: Nothing pins the "app-issued auth redirect must be a `replace`" invariant, so a future `<Navigate to="/login">` silently becomes guard-refusable again
samples.evidence: The delta elevates "an app-issued redirect has to *be* a replace, `<Navigate replace>` included, since `<Navigate>` defaults to a push" to an invariant (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:158-161, docs/design/sync-status.md). Its only enforcement is the `replace` prop hand-written at ten call sites (PrivateRoute.tsx:36, PublicRoute.tsx:24, document-detail.tsx:863, board-detail.tsx:252, docs-detail.tsx:342, notes-detail.tsx:369, slides-detail.tsx:947, file-detail.tsx:242,247, home-or-redirect.tsx:26). Dropping the prop on any of them is invisible to every mechanical lane (frontend has no `tsc`; eslint has no rule for it; the guard suite only exercises a hand-written `<Link to="/login" replace>` fixture at tests/components/navigation-guard/navigation-guard.test.tsx:60), and the resulting auth redirect becomes refusable by the unsaved-changes dialog — the exact case the guard cannot answer, since a "Stay" on an expired session leaves the user parked in a route their session no longer reaches. A rendering test for `PrivateRoute` with a registered guard, or a lint rule requiring `replace` on `<Navigate to="/login">`, would close it.

verdict.reason: Every element of the chain is present as described. `redirectTo` latches `isRedirecting = true` before assigning `window.location.href` (api/auth.ts:27-31) and a repo-wide grep shows the flag is never cleared (only three occurrences: declaration, early-return, assignment). The 401 branch of `fetchWithAuth` relies solely on that redirect for session eviction (api/auth.ts:153-161). `SyncStatusChip` registers a `beforeunload` handler that calls `event.preventDefault()`/`returnValue=''` whenever the document has unsent edits (sync-status-chip.tsx:92-103), which makes a script-initiated `location.href` assignment refusable; answering "Stay" aborts the navigation while the latch remains set for the life of the tab, so every later 401 early-returns at auth.ts:28. Callers deliberately swallow the thrown `AuthExpiredError` (template-landing.tsx:116, file-shell.tsx:91, share-dialog.tsx:92), so nothing else surfaces the expiry. The router-side fallback does not cover it: PrivateRoute only redirects when `me` is falsy (PrivateRoute.tsx:22-37), and a failed refetch retains prior data, leaving the authenticated shell and previously fetched document content rendered after session expiry. The PR's own stated invariant (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:151-165) — app-issued redirects must not be refusable — is violated by this non-router path. This is an auth/session-eviction failure with sensitive-data exposure on a shared machine, squarely in the security lane; no refutation ground applies.
